title: Firm Heterogeneity and the Response of Investment to Monetary Policy - Liberty Street Economics
gist: NY Fed staff find firm investment responds little to monetary policy in most firm-quarters but very strongly in a few, with sensitivity transient within firms and concentrated in small, young firms.

insights.claim: Investment by most firms in most quarters responds little to monetary policy, though all firms cut investment when rates rise.
insights.speaker: Thomas Drechsel
insights.so_what: Average rate-sensitivity estimates overstate typical firm response; transmission is lumpy.
insights.quote: investment by most firms in most time periods responds little to monetary policy

insights.claim: For about 5% of firm-quarters, a 1 percentage point rise in the fed funds rate from a monetary shock cuts capital growth by 4 percentage points.
insights.speaker: Thomas Drechsel
insights.so_what: A small tail of firms drives much of the aggregate investment response to hikes.

insights.claim: Policy analysis should consider the entire distribution of investment responses rather than the average effect.
insights.speaker: Thomas Drechsel
insights.so_what: Aggregate investment reaction to Fed moves depends on how many firms are in the sensitive tail at the time.

insights.claim: Most variation in firms' sensitivity to rate surprises is within firms over time, so a firm can respond strongly in one quarter and little in the next quarters.
insights.speaker: Thomas Drechsel
insights.so_what: Sensitivity is transient; hard to screen stocks by durable rate sensitivity.

insights.claim: Small and young firms cut investment the most after a monetary tightening, and firms with shorter debt maturity are also more sensitive.
insights.speaker: Thomas Drechsel
insights.so_what: Small-cap and young-firm capex is the most exposed to Fed hikes.

insights.claim: Firms reporting more optimism cut investment less after a rate hike, and perceived discount rates correlate with responsiveness, pointing to behavioral mechanisms; much of the variation stays unexplained.
insights.speaker: Thomas Drechsel
insights.so_what: Expectations and sentiment shape transmission beyond balance-sheet traits.
